welcome_page.title: Walking – Your trips and safety
welcome_page.description:
A few questions about walking, also with a pushchair, a cane or another aid, or in a wheelchair. If you rarely walk, we only ask why.

Taking part is voluntary and you can skip any question. Your answers are not linked to your name, and no public authority receives them.

Learn more about SmartUrbanity

Only the SmartUrbanity research team reads your answers. We keep them for research for 36 months; then we delete them or make them anonymous.

questions.text: In a typical week, do you make at least one trip where you walk or use a wheelchair most of the way?
questions.help: Walking here also means walking with a pushchair, a cane or another aid.

options.text: No, only short bits (e.g. to a stop or the car) or not at all

questions.text: Why do you rarely walk? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The places I go are too far or walking takes too long
Walking is tiring or physically difficult for me
I feel unsafe because of traffic
I am afraid of crime, such as theft
The streets are uncomfortable for walking (sidewalks, shade, benches)

questions.text: How far can you walk, or go in your wheelchair, without a long rest?
questions.help: A long rest means stopping for more than about 5 minutes. A rough idea is enough.

options.text: Distance is not a limit for me (e.g. power wheelchair)
I cannot walk or move around, even with a mobility aid

questions.text: In a typical week, on how many days do you walk, or go in your wheelchair, for at least 10 minutes at a time?
questions.help: Count every kind of walk: to get somewhere, for leisure or for exercise.

questions.text: How would you describe your physical fitness for walking at the moment (strength, stamina, balance)?
questions.help: Think of strength, stamina and general health.

questions.text: In the same trip, do you usually combine walking with another way of travelling?
questions.help: For example walking a good part of the way and then taking a bus or a train.

questions.text: Which other ways of travelling do you use in the same trip? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Taxi or similar service (e.g. Uber, Bolt)

questions.text: What difficulties do you experience when combining different transport modes (e.g. bike + public transport, car + metro, walking + bus)?

options.text: Vehicles are too crowded (e.g. no space for a bicycle or luggage)
Poor coordination between modes (long waiting times, missed connections)
Lack of infrastructure (e.g. no bicycle parking or no bicycle access on public transport)
Complicated transfers (stations far apart, unclear routes)
Cost is too high when combining modes
Services are infrequent or do not run in the evening
Physical effort is too high (e.g. carrying a bicycle or walking long distances)
I do not experience significant difficulties

questions.text: When you face these difficulties, how do you mostly respond?

options.text: I stop using one of the modes (e.g. stop bringing my bike)
I switch to a single mode (e.g. only car, only public transport)
I change the time of travel (e.g. avoid peak hours)
I change the route or transfer point
I choose a different combination of modes
I continue using the same combination despite difficulties
I reduce how often I make that trip
I look for alternative solutions (e.g. bike sharing instead of own bike)
I avoid that trip entirely if possible
I do not experience significant difficulties

questions.text: When you walk or use a wheelchair along roads with fast or heavy traffic, do you feel unsafe?
When you cross roads with fast or heavy traffic on foot, do you feel unsafe?
Do you make longer detours or avoid some streets because you cannot cross them safely on foot?
When you cross the street on foot, do you feel rushed or unsure?
When you walk or use a wheelchair, do you feel unsafe when cyclists or e-scooter riders pass close to you?
When you walk or use a wheelchair, do poor sidewalk conditions (e.g., holes, uneven surfaces, or crumbling edges) make you feel unsafe?
Do obstacles on the sidewalk (e.g., roadworks, bins, or parked scooters) force you to walk closer to traffic?
Do obstacles on the sidewalk (e.g., roadworks, bins, or parked scooters) force you to change your path or make a detour?
When you walk or use a wheelchair, who on the road makes you feel unsafe? (Select all that apply)
questions.help: Think of specific behaviour, such as passing too close or not giving way, rather than everyone in a group.

questions.text: When you walk or use a wheelchair, which of these situations make you feel unsafe? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Unsafe behaviour from drivers, riders or pedestrians
Lack of safe or adequate sidewalks, crossings or lighting

questions.text: Which of these do you find on your walking route? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Steps or steep curbs without ramps
Dropped kerbs at crossings missing or broken
Paths too narrow for a wheelchair, pushchair or two people to pass
Tactile paving for people with visual impairments missing or broken
Low branches or bushes taking up space
Stairs as the only way through, or stairways closed
Stretches with no sidewalk, so you have to walk in the road
Pedestrian traffic lights out of order
Pedestrian traffic lights without an audible signal

questions.text: During the day, do you ever feel unsafe from crime or harassment when you walk or use a wheelchair? (Harassment includes unwanted comments, following, touching, or intimidating behaviour directed at you.)
In the evening or after dark, do you ever feel unsafe from crime or harassment when you walk or use a wheelchair?
When you feel unsafe in the evening, what do you change?
questions.help: You can choose more than one answer.

options.text: I share my location with someone
I ask someone to come with me
I use a different means of transport

questions.text: After dark, does poor street lighting make you change your route or the time you go out on foot?
When you walk or use a wheelchair, what makes you feel less secure from crime or harassment? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Places with few people around (isolated or deserted areas)
People behaving aggressively or in an intimidating way
Poor maintenance (e.g. abandoned buildings, graffiti, broken infrastructure)
No surveillance or security measures (e.g. no cameras, no staff)
Incidents that happened to me or were reported in the area
Few cues to find my way without sight (e.g. no tactile paths or audio announcements)
Not being able to hear people or vehicles approaching

questions.text: When you walk or use a wheelchair, have you experienced or do you fear harassment because of who you are or how you look (e.g. gender, appearance, origin, age, disability)?
